plays.title: Interview the first-customer story
plays.description: Maya's public work is a weekly conversation with a founder about how the first customers actually arrived. The play is to borrow that format: one guest, one acquisition channel, one tactic a viewer can try this week.
plays.action: Record or write one founder conversation. Open with the channel they used, name the experiment that failed, and end with a single tactic. Publish it where your buyers already watch or read.
plays.example: BuildingNow.fm leads with founder episodes such as Jay Yang on cold email and Elitza Vasileva on a Product Hunt launch, plus a 7-day first-customer plan on the show site.

plays.title: Put the lesson on owned media
plays.description: The X bio points at the podcast and the YouTube archive, and buildwithmaya.com collects the weekly lessons. X introduces the episode. The email and the show site keep it.
plays.action: Publish the long version on a site or newsletter you control. Use X only for the hook, the guest name, and the link. Repeat the same URL in the profile.
plays.example: Her X profile links BuildingNow.fm and the YouTube archive, and buildwithmaya.com offers the weekly lessons by email.

plays.title: Ship the tool you needed
plays.description: IdeaPanda and Newbie Marketer are still live next to the show. The pattern is to turn a personal marketing problem into a small product, then let the interviews supply the distribution lessons.

plays.title: Report one experiment

plays.action: Once a week, post one distribution experiment with the channel, the action, and the result. If it failed, say what you will change next week.
plays.example: buildwithmaya.com describes weekly experiments and founder insights, after she writes that marketing burnout led her to learn distribution in public.

Put the long lesson somewhere you own. Let X only carry the hook and the link.
